title: Diwali 2026 in Dubai: Where to Shop, What to Buy and How Not to Overspend
excerpt: Meena Bazaar for outfits and diyas, the Deira Gold Souk on Dhanteras, and a Dubai Jewellery Group campaign with 1 kg of gold in raffles running October 24 to November 12 — a practical guide for the Gulf diaspora, with Diwali on Sunday, November 8.
body:
• Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8 in 2026, with Dhanteras on November 6 — the biggest gold-buying day, when the Deira Gold Souk and Meena Bazaar jewellers see their largest crowds.
  • Meena Bazaar in Bur Dubai — Dubai's Little India since the 1970s — is the one-stop district for lehengas, kurtas, diyas, rangoli powders, torans and mithai.
  • The Dubai Jewellery Group's Diwali campaign runs October 24 to November 12 across participating jewellers, with raffles totalling 1 kg of gold.
  • Personal fireworks are prohibited in the UAE — only licensed official displays are allowed. Order tailoring early: Meena Bazaar stitchers are swamped in the final week.

Dubai does Diwali at scale, and the shopping has a geography every resident learns: Bur Dubai for clothes and decorations, Deira for gold, and the malls for everything else. With the main celebration falling on a Sunday this year, residents can plan festivities around the weekend, according to Dubai Standard's Diwali 2026 shopping guide.

Meena Bazaar: the one-trip district

Located in Bur Dubai around Al Fahidi Street and Khalid Bin Al Waleed Road, Meena Bazaar has been a shopping destination for the Indian community since the 1970s and becomes particularly lively during Diwali, with stores displaying colourful garments, jewellery and decorative items. Traditional clothing runs from lehengas, salwar suits and kurtis to sherwanis, kurta-pyjama sets and festive outfits for children. Shoppers can select fabrics and have outfits stitched to measure — but tailoring shops are particularly busy before Diwali, so ordering early is advisable.

"Dubai does Diwali at scale, and the shopping has a geography every resident learns: Bur Dubai for clothes and decorations, Deira for gold, and the malls for everything else."

The same streets cover home decoration — clay diyas, decorative lighting, torans and rangoli powders, often at competitive prices compared with larger malls — and festive food, with outlets such as Kailash Parbat and Royal Sweets offering chaat, mithai and other Indian favourites. For shoppers combining clothing, decorations and food in a single trip, Meena Bazaar is the convenient answer.

Gold: Dhanteras discipline

Across Dubai Creek, the Deira Gold Souk experiences its busiest night on Dhanteras, when many families traditionally buy gold. The Dubai Jewellery Group's Diwali campaign runs October 24 to November 12, 2026 across participating jewellers, with festive offers and raffles totalling 1 kg of gold, according to UAE Mercury's Diwali guide. Dubai's gold price recently dipped below Dh500 per gram for 24K in mid-October reporting — 24-carat traded at Dh481.5 per gram on Saturday, October 24 in the rates cited there, against Dh512.25 during Diwali last year — pulling festive buying forward. Prices move daily, so check the day's rate before you shop.

How not to overspend, in practice: fix the gram weight before you enter the souk, compare the making charges (that is where jewellers differ most), and treat raffles as a bonus, never as a reason to buy more metal than planned.

Temples and the rules

Dubai's main Hindu temple is now the Hindu Temple Dubai in Jebel Ali, in the Worship Village, opened in October 2022 and home to 16 deities; the old Bur Dubai Shiva Mandir relocated there in January 2024, while the Krishna Mandir remains at the original Bur Dubai complex near the Dubai Museum. Both draw very large crowds across the Diwali days, and the Jebel Ali temple has used online registration and QR entry on peak days — check the temple's official site before you go and arrive early.

One firm rule for newcomers: personal fireworks and firecrackers are prohibited in the UAE. Only licensed official displays are allowed — plan your celebration around the city's official fireworks and the diyas, not around anything bought for the purpose.
